newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals says 1997 M3 growth guideline achievable.
newsitem.headline: Stals says 1997 M3 growth guideline achievable.

text.p: Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals told reporters on Tuesday that South Africa should be able to meet the guideline of keeping M3 money supply growth below 10 percent in 1997.
"We think the guideline of up to 10 percent will not be unrealistic for this year," Stals said.
The central bank would be helped in its goal by the fact that South African companies had more access to foreign financing which would reduce local bank credit extension, he said.
Preliminary South African money supply growth in December last year was 13.73 percent, while growth in credit extension to the private sector was 15.75 percent.

Quarter-to-quarter growth in credit extension at seasonally adjusted and annualised rates, decelerated from 22.4 percent in the second quarter of 1996 to 16.6 percent in the third quarter, and 11.8 percent in the fourth quarter.
In the case of M3 money supply, the deceleration was from 21.2 percent in the second quarter, to 18.6 percent in the third, and a mere 7.6 percent in the fourth.
Commenting on the continued high money market shortage, Stals said the Reserve Bank was deliberately keeping liquidity tight to bear down on excessive bank credit extension and money supply growth.
"We deliberately keep the money market short at this stage," he said.
